title: View-first task allocation versus PackNet-style masks
hypothesis: In a sequential task stream with five tasks on one shared Givens orbit followed by three unrelated tasks, a Mirror-first allocator delays private readout allocation for more tasks than a packed binary-mask/PackNet-style allocator, while preserving all prior task functions and reducing complete serialized bytes.
physical_object: one shared 32-value readout over a fixed deterministic 16-to-32 ReLU feature encoder
mirror_coordinate: one int8 scalar angle per accepted task over a fixed pairwise Givens schedule; private float32 readout fallback when validation fails
logical_multiplicity: eight sequential task functions: five aligned, three unrelated
controls: PackNet-style packed binary mask followed by private-readout allocation

task.stream_order: five Givens-aligned tasks then three unrelated task vectors
task.metric: mean normalized held-out MSE across all seen tasks
task.retention_audit: re-evaluate every earlier task after each new task allocation

development.selection_metric: smallest validation threshold accepting all five aligned tasks while rejecting unrelated tasks to private allocation
development.selection_reason: At 0.001 both development worlds accepted all five aligned tasks and rejected all three unrelated tasks. Threshold 0.0001 caused one aligned private fallback; 0.01 did not improve allocation or quality over 0.001.

fresh.access_condition: Development selected one frozen threshold; fresh reports allocation events, retention, quality and complete payload bytes without retuning.

training.optimizer: least-squares support fit plus deterministic coordinate/grid search

storage.authority: actual complete compact serialized inference payload bytes
storage.serialization: uint16 JSON-header length plus little-endian state tensors and compact per-task allocation records
paid_objects: every accepted angle code or packed mask

gates.promising: In all three fresh worlds: Mirror accepts all five aligned tasks without private weights, allocates private readouts only for unrelated tasks, retains earlier tasks within 1e-6 normalized MSE, and reduces total payload at least 20% vs PackNet-style masks plus allocation at no more than 1.25x measured allocation-search time.
gates.fail: Mirror allocates aligned tasks privately in >=2 fresh worlds, retention exceeds 1e-4, or complete bytes are not at least 10% lower than PackNet-style allocation in >=2 fresh worlds.
gates.not_established: invalid split, serializer mismatch, or incomplete worlds

boundaries: synthetic linear readout stream over fixed random features
PackNet-style mask/allocate control is a small linear allocation analogue, not a full Transformer PackNet reproduction
no continual optimizer training or language-model claim
